text: Auto-pairing by (object, name) false-pairs sibling member triggers (two OnAction / field OnValidate triggers share name and signatureFingerprint but have member-discriminated ids). Equal hashes then hide the ABI change and the other passes compare two different triggers as one subject.
evidence: Verified: src/engine/ids.rs:324-336 hashes the member into the id; tests/cli-b-goldens/snapshot/ws-sibling-member-triggers.raw.json has two OnAction facts with equal signatureFingerprint and different stableIds. The member is hashed and cannot be recovered, so it cannot join the key. design-r1: candidates must be member-less (stableId == object#signatureFingerprint) AND a pair needs old signatureFingerprint != new. Oracle A2e; the discrimination limit of the two redundant guards is stated.

text: The events pass reads raw old routine ids from declaration bodies, but the capability map is keyed by normalized ids. A paired local [EventSubscriber] with an unchanged write would produce a false event-subscriber-induced-capability-gained.
re_raise: Round 2 (sol): a third raw-old-id site was missed. When the publisher is gone from new, the subscriber-induced findings use the old publisher's raw routine as their subject (passes.rs:726-732).
evidence: Round 1 verified passes.rs:791-818 (writes_of), indexes.rs:195-222 and passes.rs:570-582. Round 2 verified passes.rs:726-732: `new_publishers.get(key).or_else(|| old_publishers.get(key)).and_then(|d| get_str(d, "routine"))` reads the raw old id on the fallback. design-r2 Details (d) lists three sites, all going through DiffIndexes::normalize_old. New oracle A2g asserts that the subscriber-induced finding's subject is the paired NEW id. New discrimination: drop normalize_old at that fallback, and A2g fails.

text: Gaps in the tests and discrimination proofs. A2b cannot detect broken old-coverage normalization under the loose policy. BusinessEvent, publisher-attribute contraction and paired-event behaviour are untested. Synthetic attribute facts do not pin production attribute (or routineKind) emission.
evidence: design-r1 changes: A2b now also runs under CoveragePolicy::Strict, with old coverage keyed by the OLD id. A1c has a BusinessEvent case. A1e covers dropping the attribute and replacing it with InternalEvent. A2f covers a paired subscriber. The new ws-mode fixture E2E-2 pins the production routineKind and attribute emission. Each has a listed discrimination proof.

text: Triggers (object/field/action) carry no access modifier, so they map to visibility public and remain ABI. Adding an action gives procedure-added and removing one gives a critical procedure-removed, which inflates CentralGauge's abi_changes.
evidence: Conductor decision: in scope. Verified: snapshot_full.rs:714-723; ModelRoutine.kind (workspace.rs:445-447). design-r1: derive_contracts emits routineKind (additive, no bump), and is_abi_surface marks a trigger as not ABI. Oracle A1f, fixture E2E-2; golden moves updated.

text: The event-attribute check must ignore case: snapshot attribute names are case-preserved as written.
evidence: Verified: snapshot_full.rs:728-731; program/attributes.rs:47. design-r1 uses eq_ignore_ascii_case; A1c has a lowercase case, with a discrimination proof.

text: ExternalBusinessEvent publishers are usually local and are an external contract; they are missing from the publisher exception.
evidence: design-r1 exception set: IntegrationEvent, BusinessEvent, ExternalBusinessEvent. The check reads attributes, not routineKind, because classify_kind_ir (src/engine/snapshot.rs:91-110) does not mark ExternalBusinessEvent. A1c case plus a discrimination proof.

text: (M2 + M3a, merged) The 'user overlay wins' rule had no test that could fail. Merging auto pairs into the table that goes through validate_overlay_against_snapshots could give false rename-overlay-stale diagnostics.
re_raise: Round 2 (sol): the claimed 'validate the merged table' discrimination cannot fail. A2d creates no auto pair, and valid auto endpoints are already in identities (renames.rs:116-123).
evidence: Round 2 verified: the stale check tests membership in identities.stableIds (renames.rs:116-123, fed by indexes.rs:246-260). A pairing candidate needs its display name from that same identities array, so both ends of an auto pair are always in stableIds and can never be reported stale. design-r2 Details (c) drops the filtering (no code: the merged table goes through the existing check unchanged), states why it cannot be observed, and retracts the discrimination claim. The overlay-wins half stays as before: A2d (stale user entry plus a same-name new-only routine) with the 'drop the user-table exclusion' proof.

text: (final r1) Duplicate contract rows (same stable id twice) defeat pairing: the (object,name) group becomes 2:1 and the pair is lost.
evidence: Verified: build_diff_indexes keys contract facts by stableId with IndexMap insert (last wins), while routine_rows returned a Vec. routine_rows now returns IndexMap<stableId, RoutineRow> (last wins). Regression issue156_fq01_duplicate_rows_still_pair: with renames.rs at 41c191ee it FAILS (removed d1 + added d2); with the fix it passes.

text: (CR-4) Pairing ignored ABI status: public Foo removed + local Foo added became object-accessibility-narrowed + procedure-signature-changed instead of a critical procedure-removed.
evidence: The pairing key is now (object, lowercased name, is_abi_surface). issue156_fq02_abi_status_change_is_not_a_pair asserts exactly [procedure-removed #f1] critical. Proof: key forced to `true || self.abi` -> FAIL (narrowed + signature-changed); at 41c191ee also FAIL; reverted -> pass. Side effect: a local -> public change together with a signature change is now removed (nothing) + procedure-added, which is the correct ABI view.

text: (CR-1) An internal event publisher should be non-ABI (subscribable only in-app/friends).
evidence: Microsoft Learn, AppSourceCop AS0025 (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/analyzers/appsourcecop-as0025, updated 2026-10-07): 'Dependent extensions can subscribe to these events, even if the events are marked with the local or internal access modifiers. The access modifier only limits the ability to raise the event.' So internal publishers ARE the contract, and the existing rule (event attribute before visibility) is right. Pinned: issue156_a1c now loops local AND internal for all four attributes. Proof: `visibility != internal && (...)` -> FAIL '[IntegrationEvent] internal publisher removal is an ABI break'; reverted -> pass. is_abi_surface doc cites AS0025.

text: (opus M2 = sol 2) The EventPublisherRemoved subject normalization (site 2) had no assertion.
evidence: A2g now also asserts event-publisher-removed subject == #p2. Proof: passes.rs site 2 without normalize_old -> FAIL ('the removed publisher's subject is the paired new id', left #p1); reverted -> pass.

text: (opus M1) The ledger claimed the new-side user-target exclusion is untestable; a stale overlay X->T (X absent from old, T in new) plus an old-only T' of the same name exercises it.
evidence: Oracle issue156_fq05_user_target_never_auto_pairs (overlay #x->#t, old #tp 'W', new #t 'W') expects removed #tp + added #t. Proof: drop `!user_targets.contains(..)` -> FAIL (signature-changed #t); reverted -> pass. Stated limit (CHANGELOG + ledger, one-hop normalization): an old id the overlay maps to a target missing from new stays a removal (A2d). Chains are NOT excluded: with user X->T, an old-only routine whose own id is T and a new-only same-name U, the auto pair T->U is allowed (renames.rs:172-179 checks only the old id against user KEYS). Normalization is one hop, so X's facts land on T (not followed to U) and old T's facts land on U.
re_raise: Final round 2 (sol): the claim 'auto entries never chain with user entries' was false — user X->T + old-only T + new-only same-name U permits auto T->U (renames.rs:172-179). Wording corrected to the documented one-hop limitation; code and test unchanged.

Proof now discriminates on one guard: member-less filter forced true -> FAIL a2e (sibling OnActions paired); reverted -> pass.
